nodes.summary: Given a list $l$ of attributes and a set $S$ of attributes, the candidate violations of BCNF in $S$ are all subsets of the set of attributes that occur in $l$ and lie in $S$, listed once each. Duplicates in $l$ are removed first, so there are $2^k$ candidates when $k$ distinct attributes of $l$ lie in $S$.
nodes.title: Candidate BCNF violations

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a set of functional dependencies, $l$ a list of attributes, $n$ a natural number and $S$ a scheme. For $n = 0$ the result is the list $[S]$. For $n > 0$, the candidate violations of BCNF in $S$ built from $l$ are searched in order for the first $X$ that violates BCNF in $S$ for $F$. If there is none, the result is $[S]$. Otherwise, with $X^+$ the attribute closure of $X$ under $F$, the result is the…
nodes.title: BCNF decomposition with bounded depth

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a set of functional dependencies, $l$ a list of attributes and $S$ a set of attributes, and let $r$ be a relation over $S$ that satisfies every dependency $X \to Y$ derivable from $F$ with $X, Y \subseteq S$. Then $r$ is the natural join of its projections onto the schemes of the BCNF decomposition of $S$ for $F$ and $l$.
nodes.title: The BCNF decomposition is lossless

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a set of functional dependencies, $l$ a list of attributes and $S$ a scheme. The BCNF decomposition of $S$ for $F$ and $l$ is the BCNF decomposition with bounded depth run on $S$ with depth bound $|S|$. At each step, if some candidate violation of BCNF in the current scheme $T$ built from $l$ violates BCNF in $T$ for $F$, the first such $X$ is used: with $X^+$ the attribute closure of $X$ under $F$, $T$…
nodes.title: BCNF decomposition

nodes.summary: A list $l$ of schemes is dependency-preserving for a set $F$ of functional dependencies when every dependency of $F$ is derivable from the union, over the schemes $S$ of $l$, of the sets of dependencies $X \to Y$ derivable from $F$ with $X, Y \subseteq S$.
nodes.title: Dependency-preserving decompositions

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a set of functional dependencies, let $R_1$ and $R_2$ be schemes whose union is the set of all attributes, and let $D$ be a value type containing at least two distinct elements. If the decomposition of $R_1 \cup R_2$ into $R_1$ and $R_2$ is lossless for $F$ with values in $D$, then $F$ derives $R_1 \cap R_2 \to R_1$ or $R_1 \cap R_2 \to R_2$.
nodes.title: Converse of the lossless-join test for two schemes

nodes.summary: Two sets $F$ and $G$ of functional dependencies are equivalent when $F$ derives every dependency of $G$ and $G$ derives every dependency of $F$.
nodes.title: Equivalent sets of functional dependencies

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a set of functional dependencies and $l$ a list containing every attribute. Then for every scheme $S$, every scheme in the BCNF decomposition of $S$ for $F$ and $l$ is in Boyce–Codd normal form for $F$.
nodes.title: The BCNF decomposition produces BCNF schemes

nodes.summary: A scheme $S$ is in Boyce–Codd normal form for a set $F$ of functional dependencies when, for every dependency $X \to Y$ derivable from $F$ with $X, Y \subseteq S$, either $Y \subseteq X$ or $F$ derives $X \to S$ (that is, $X$ is a superkey of $S$).
nodes.title: Boyce–Codd normal form

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a set of functional dependencies and $S$ a scheme, and write $X^+$ for the attribute closure of a set $X$ of attributes under $F$. A set $X \subseteq S$ violates BCNF in $S$ when $S \not\subseteq X^+$ and $X^+ \cap S \not\subseteq X$, that is, when the closure $X^+ \cap S$ of $X$ within $S$ is neither $X$ nor $S$.
nodes.title: BCNF violations

nodes.summary: If the dependency `R₁ ∩ R₂ → R₁` holds in a relation `r` over `R₁ ∪ R₂`, then `r` is the natural join of its projections onto `R₁` and `R₂`.
nodes.title: Heath's theorem

nodes.summary: For a relation $r$ (a finite set of tuples) and a list of schemes $S_1, \dots, S_n$, this is the natural join of the projections $\pi_{S_1} r, \dots, \pi_{S_n} r$, computed as $\pi_{S_1} r \bowtie (\pi_{S_2} r \bowtie (\cdots \bowtie (\pi_{S_n} r \bowtie U)))$, where $U$ is the relation containing only the empty tuple; for the empty list it is $U$.
nodes.title: Join of the projections of a relation

nodes.summary: The relation containing only the empty tuple, the unit of the natural join.
nodes.title: Unit relation of the natural join

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies, let $R_1$ and $R_2$ be sets of attributes whose union is the set of all attributes, and suppose that the value type $D$ has two distinct elements. Then the decomposition into $R_1$ and $R_2$ is lossless for $F$ with values in $D$ if and only if $R_1 \cap R_2 \to R_1$ or $R_1 \cap R_2 \to R_2$ is derivable from $F$ by Armstrong's axioms.
nodes.title: Lossless binary decompositions

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies and let $R_1$, $R_2$ be sets of attributes. If $R_1 \cap R_2 \to R_1$ or $R_1 \cap R_2 \to R_2$ is derivable from $F$ by Armstrong's axioms, then for every value type $D$ the decomposition of $R_1 \cup R_2$ into $R_1$ and $R_2$ is lossless for $F$ with values in $D$.
nodes.title: Lossless binary decompositions from derivable dependencies

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies, let $R_1$ and $R_2$ be finite sets of attributes, and let $D$ be a type of values. The decomposition of $R_1 \cup R_2$ into $R_1$ and $R_2$ is lossless for $F$ with values in $D$ when every relation $r$ over $R_1 \cup R_2$ with values in $D$ that satisfies $F$ on $R_1 \cup R_2$ (every dependency $X \to Y$ with $X, Y \subseteq R_1 \cup R_2$ that is derivable from…
nodes.title: Lossless decomposition into two schemes

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a relation over a schema $R$ and let $S_1, \dots, S_n$ be a list of schemes, each contained in $R$. A tuple $t$ belongs to the natural join of the projections $\pi_{S_1} r, \dots, \pi_{S_n} r$ if and only if $t$ is a tuple over $S_1 \cup \dots \cup S_n$ and, for every $i$, the restriction of $t$ to $S_i$ belongs to $\pi_{S_i} r$.
nodes.title: Membership in a join of projections

nodes.summary: For a finite set $F$ of functional dependencies and a set $S$ of attributes, this is the finite set of all dependencies $X \to Y$ with $X, Y \subseteq S$ that are derivable from $F$ by Armstrong's axioms, that is, the projection onto $S$ of the closure $F^+$ of $F$.
nodes.title: Projection of the dependency closure onto a scheme

nodes.summary: A relation $r$ satisfies a finite set $F$ of functional dependencies on a set $S$ of attributes when every dependency $X \to Y$ with $X, Y \subseteq S$ that is derivable from $F$ by Armstrong's axioms holds in $r$.
nodes.title: Satisfying a set of dependencies on a scheme

nodes.summary: For a list $S_1, \dots, S_n$ of schemes (finite sets of attributes), this is the union $S_1 \cup \dots \cup S_n$; for the empty list it is the empty set.
nodes.title: Union of a list of schemes

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies and $G$ a list of functional dependencies equivalent to $F$ (each derives every dependency of the other). Then for every set of attributes $K$, the decomposition synthesized from $G$ and $K$, with one scheme $X \cup Y$ for each dependency $X \to Y$ of $G$ together with the scheme $K$, is dependency-preserving for $F$.
nodes.title: Synthesis is dependency-preserving

nodes.summary: For a cover `G` of `F` and a superkey `K` of all attributes, every relation over all attributes satisfying `F` is the join of its projections onto the synthesized schemes.
nodes.title: Synthesis is lossless

nodes.summary: Given a list $G$ of functional dependencies and a set of attributes $K$, the synthesized decomposition is the list of schemes consisting of $K$ followed by, for each dependency $X \to Y$ of $G$ in order, the scheme $X \cup Y$.
nodes.title: Synthesis

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
